st: Mix the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Add [[1 tbsp]] oil and the water, then knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Rest for [[20 minutes]].
Divide the dough into 2 balls. Roll each into a thin 9-inch round.
Cook each chapati in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1 minute per side. Brush with oil and cook until golden and soft. Keep warm.
Beat the eggs with [[0.25 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Stir in the cabbage, tomato and onion.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat. Pour half the egg mix in and spread thin.
Cook for 2 minutes until set, flip, and cook 1 minute more. Make a second omelet.
Lay an omelet on each hot chapati and roll up tightly.
Slice in half and serve right away.

ing: or plantains, peeled and cut in chunks
st: Oil your hands and knife before peeling the bananas, because their sap stains. Put the pieces in cold water.
Heat the oil in a pot. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and beef. Brown for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, salt and pepper, and cook for 5 minutes.
Add [[1 cup]] water, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes until the beef is nearly tender.
Drain the bananas. Add them with [[2 cups]] water and stir gently.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until the matoke is soft and creamy.
Mash lightly with a spoon if you like and serve warm.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the water until smooth. Stir it into the pan.
Add the chicken and simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Pass the banana leaves briefly over a flame until soft. Cut into squares big enough to wrap.
Put a spoon of sauce and chicken in the center of each leaf. Fold into a tight parcel and tie with string.
Steam the parcels over simmering water, covered, for 1 hour 15 minutes. Chicken must reach 165°F (74°C).
Place in bowls and open the parcels at the table.
Roast the peanuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 6 minutes until lightly browned.
Rub off the skins in a towel and grind the nuts to a smooth paste in a blender with a little water.
Heat the oil in a pot. Cook the onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and salt. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Mix the peanut paste into [[2 cups]] water and add it to the pot.
Simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring often so it does not stick.
Taste and add salt if needed. Serve with matoke, rice or sweet potatoes.
Mix the flour, salt and sugar in a bowl.
Add [[2 tbsp]] oil and the warm milk slowly. Mix into a soft dough.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Divide into 8 balls. Roll each into a thin round.
Brush with a little oil, roll up into a rope, then coil it and press flat. Rest 10 minutes.
Roll out each coil into a 7-inch round.
Cook each in a hot skillet for 1 minute per side, brushing with oil, until golden brown with spots.
Stack and cover with a towel to stay soft.
Oil your hands before peeling the bananas, and soak the pieces in cold water.
Heat the oil in a pot. Cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the beef and garlic and brown for 8 minutes.
Add [[1 cup]] water and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, carrots and salt. Cook for 5 minutes.
Drain the bananas and add them with [[2 cups]] water.
Cover and cook for 20 minutes until the bananas are soft and the stew is thick.
Stir gently and serve hot for breakfast.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt.
Beat the egg with the warm coconut milk and [[1 tbsp]] oil, then add to the flour.
Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and soft.
Cover and let rise for [[1 hour]].
Roll out half an inch thick and cut into triangles.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 340°F (170°C).
Fry the mandazi for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and puffy.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm or cool.
